headline: Ransomware keeps the VPN door open while everyone else patches
standfirst: A KEV-listed PAN-OS authentication bypass with confirmed ransomware use leads today, with Qilin and INC operators still using it for initial access. Behind it: autonomous AI agents run against more than 1,200 websites, a new APT28 loader aimed at the defense industrial base, a public proof-of-concept for a critical FortiSIEM path traversal, and a Siemens DLL-sideloading flaw the vendor says is live in ClickFix lures. ConnectWise's Cloud Backup remains offline, an OVHcloud CLI release was poisoned for up to 94 minutes, and DHS has ordered DeepSeek out of federal civilian systems.
bodyMarkdown:
## Actively exploited

CVE-2026-0257 is a High-severity authentication bypass (CVSS 4.0: 7.8, CWE-565) in the GlobalProtect portal and gateway of PAN-OS, with a network-reachable vector requiring no privileges and no user interaction. The impact is narrow but valuable: bypassing security restrictions to establish an unauthorized VPN connection. Panorama and Cloud NGFW are not affected. The flaw is in CISA's KEV catalog with known ransomware campaign use, and Qilin and INC operators are reported to be using it to stand up rogue VPN sessions against a fix that has already shipped [[s3]]. CISA's required action is vendor mitigations or discontinuation of the product, with a federal remediation due date — a US federal deadline, not a universal one. Analysis: the 7.8 undersells this. A patched, KEV-listed edge-device bypass that still yields initial access for extortion crews means unpatched GlobalProtect portals remain an active entry point; the supplied reporting does not say how many remain exposed or how victims were selected.

Siemens has fixed a DLL-sideloading flaw in Software Center, CVE-2026-110936 (CVSS v4: 8.4, High, CWE-427), affecting versions below V4.0.9.8, and says it has been exploited in ClickFix attacks to deploy a remote access trojan [[s37]]. Worth reading the vector carefully: the NVD record describes an authenticated local attacker with high privileges placing a crafted DLL in a directory the application searches, so the flaw is the execution step rather than the lure — the ClickFix social-engineering stage supplies the user action the CVSS vector does not capture. It is also a confirmed KEV miss despite the vendor's exploitation statement, which is a reminder that catalog absence is not evidence of safety.

## Research

A Chinese-speaking criminal pointed autonomous AI agents at company websites with almost no human help, and the campaign is unusually well documented because the operators left their control panels exposed on the internet [[s9]]. The agents attempted more than 1,200 sites and reached websites belonging to more than 100 companies, including an industrial manufacturer and an appliance maker. No CVE is involved; the story is the economics. Analysis: agentic tooling collapses the cost of trying 1,200 targets, and the leaked panels give defenders a rare view of how the targeting was sequenced — the supplied text does not say what the agents succeeded in doing after access.

APT28 has been attributed to attacks on two NATO member states, including a breach of a naval shipbuilder, deploying a backdoor called HOOKEDGE alongside a previously unseen reflective loader; researchers track the cluster as Swallowtail [[s30]]. For anyone defending the defense industrial base, the loader and backdoor are the actionable part — new tooling means existing signatures are the wrong place to look.

## Vulnerabilities

A public proof-of-concept now exists for CVE-2026-106173, a path traversal (CWE-22) in FortiSIEM that permits unauthenticated remote code execution [[s2]]. The severity figures in the supplied material disagree: reporting gives 9.4, while the NVD record carries CVSS 3.1 at 9.8 — both Critical, and the NVD description names FortiSIEM 7.5.0. Either way this is a patch-now item for anything exposing the platform, because the PoC lowers the skill floor. It is a confirmed KEV miss; the supplied evidence does not report in-the-wild exploitation, and the PoC's mechanics are not described.

## Breaches

ConnectWise says it has strengthened administrative-access protections and is resetting accounts and replacing application credentials after unauthorized access to application identities associated with Cloud Backup, which remains offline [[s31]]. Analysis: the unresolved question for partners is downstream — MSP tooling and Microsoft 365 tenant exposure is what should be scoped now. The supplied material does not state whether customer data was accessed or how many partners are affected.

An attacker used a hijacked contributor account to replace the download archives on five existing OVHcloud CLI releases with a build designed to steal secrets stored on disk [[s36]]. The malicious files were live for up to 94 minutes, from 12:47 to 14:21 UTC. Short windows are not reassuring here: mirror caches and CI pipelines that pulled during that gap keep the tainted artifact long after the releases were pulled.

## Industry

DHS is ordering federal civilian agencies to stop using DeepSeek products and remove them from government systems [[s7]]. Analysis: policy-driven removal of AI tooling sets an expectation that extends past the agencies themselves — contractors handling federal work should assume the same posture is coming. No effective date, scope exemptions or enforcement mechanism are in the supplied excerpt.

nvd.description: This is a vulnerability in Bitbucket Data Center, Confluence Data Center, Jira Service Management Data Center, Jira Software Data Center, Bamboo Data Center. Crowd Data Center, Crucible and Fisheye. This Arbitrary File Access vulnerability allows an unauthenticated attacker to access specific files within the web application root directory in affected versions. Exploitation requires prior knowledge of the target file's exact name and path; this vulnerability does not allow attackers to enumerate or list directory contents. In some configurations, there may be some sensitive files that make this highly severe. This vulnerability allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to access specific files within the web application root directory in affected versions. The vulnerability must be addressed for affected versions of: -- Bitbucket Data Center, introduced in version >= 4.6.0, fix versions: 9.4.26, 10.2.8, 10.5.1 -- Confluence Data Center, introduced in version >= 5.10.0, fix versions 9.2.26, 10.2.19 -- Crowd Data Center, introduced in version >= 2.11.0, fix versions 6.3.7, 7.0.3, 7.1.7, 7.2.4 -- Jira Software Data Center, introduced in version >= 7.1.0, fix versions 9.12.40, 10.3.26, 11.3.12 -- Jira Service Management Data Center, introduced in version >= 3.1.0, fix versions 5.12.40, 10.3.26, 11.3.12 -- Bamboo Data Center >= 7.0.1, fix versions 10.2.24, 12.1.12 -- Crucible, fix versions 4.9.15 -- Fisheye, fix version 4.9.15 -- Exploitation requires prior knowledge of the target file's exact name and path.
